family: Collatz-like (4q/3) cycles of a counter machine on runs of 11010 and 110
summary: A counter machine on runs of 11010 and 110 that runs in cycles: the main counter q follows 3q' = 4q + c with a small correction c set by a short tail, so it grows by about 4/3 per cycle (q = 69, 95, 133, 178, 239, 323, 433, 579, 777, 1039); open.
title: What is known about 1RB1RC_1LC0LF_1RF0LD_0RE1LB_1RC---_1LD0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RC_1LC0LF_1RF0LD_0RE1LB_1RC---_1LD0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The tape is a few long runs of three words and a block of 1s, and the machine runs in cycles in which the main counter follows a Collatz-like map q' = (4q + c)/3, with a small correction c decided by a short tail at the right end. The tail's rule is not known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 26,735 cells have been visited and 17,233 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L (11010)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (01101)^n R; L (110)^n B> 1 R reaches L B> 1 (110)^n R; L F> (110)^n R reaches L (011)^n F> R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L (11010)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (01101)^n R; L (110)^n B> 1 R reaches L B> 1 (110)^n R; L F> (110)^n R reaches L (011)^n F> R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: The cycle map in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: At each of the 10 complete cycles (12 cycle starts) in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps the counters satisfy 3q' = 4q + c with c in {2, 5, 7, 9, 13, 15, 17, 19}, n' + q' = n + 2q + d with |d| ≤ 2, and r' = 2q' + e with e in [−9, 3], read off the tape at the D-visits of the left end.

claims.title: Shift rules
claims.text: For every length n of the run and any tape around it: L (11010)^n D> 1 R reaches L D> 1 (01101)^n R; L (110)^n B> 1 R reaches L B> 1 (110)^n R; L F> (110)^n R reaches L (011)^n F> R. These are the moves the head makes across the long uniform stretches of the tape.

claims.title: The cycle map in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: At each of the 12 complete cycles (13 cycle starts) in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps the counters satisfy 3q' = 4q + c with c in {2, 5, 7, 9, 13, 15, 17, 19}, n' + q' = n + 2q + d with |d| ≤ 2, and r' = 2q' + e with e in [−9, 3], read off the tape at the D-visits of the left end.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. It halts exactly when state E reads a 1; with the transfer rules unknown, nothing is known about when that could happen.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine writes almost its whole tape as a few long runs of three short words, so it is really juggling a handful of large numbers. It works in cycles, and in each cycle its main number is multiplied by about 4/3, with a small correction: a Collatz-like rule.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
The main counter at the start of each cycle, exactly, with c small.
Crossing runs of 11010 and of 110, proved for every length.

sections.heading: A counter machine in disguise
html: Write a = 11010 and b = 110. At step 109 the tape reads
1 0 a^1230 b 1 a^1474 1 a (b a a)^113 (b a) 1 (b a)^1162 b 0 1^2320 a (b a a) (b a)^2 1 b b 1^5 b^3 …
a few long runs and a short tail at the right end that hardly grows. Each run length is a counter, and Lean proves how the head crosses runs of a and of b for every length.

sections.heading: Multiply by 4/3, plus a little
html: The run is a sequence of cycles. A cycle starts when the head, at the left end, sees 0 0 b a^n b (b a a) (b a)^q b X 1^r T. In the first phase, every two visits of the left end turn one (b a) into two more as and two more 1s (n + 2, q − 1, r + 2). In the second, the head walks back one a per visit, building runs of (b a a) and (b a), until the next cycle starts:

At every cycle, exactly, 3q′ = 4q + c with a small c (between 2 and 19), n′ + q′ = n + 2q ± 2 and r′ ≈ 2q′. So the main counter obeys a Collatz-like rule, q′ = (4q + c)/3, and grows by about 4/3 per cycle; each cycle takes about 1.8 times as long as the one before. The small corrections are set by the tail, which each cycle rewrites a little, a record of the remainders, much like the stack of 1RB1RA_1LC0RB_…. A halt (state E reading a 1) would have to come from the tail.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496). Right of the start it stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half).
After 109 steps the tape spans 26,735 cells (19,632 left of the start, 62 right), with a density of 1s of 0.645.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.
